tldr: AUTORULE automatically extracts alignment rules from LLM-generated reasoning chains on preference data and uses them as an auxiliary rule-based reward during GRPO training, improving preference alignment and reducing reward hacking.
contributions: Introduction of AUTORULE, a framework for automatic extraction of alignment rules from preference data via LLM-generated reasoning chains
Demonstration that rule-based rewards derived via AUTORULE improve preference alignment and instruction following compared to standard baselines
Evidence that AUTORULE reduces reward hacking and yields interpretable, dataset-adaptive rules
methods: Given preference pairs, a reasoning model (Deepseek-R1) generates step-by-step justifications for why one response is preferred. Explicit rules are extracted individually from each reasoning chain, aggregated across examples, and merged into a compact final rule set (reduced to ~1-2% of original size). During training, a verifier (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) scores each output as binary rule satisfaction, producing a mean rule score as auxiliary reward combined with the learned reward model. This composite reward is used within the GRPO algorithm for policy optimization.
results: Training Llama-3-8B with AUTORULE achieves a 28.6% relative improvement in length-controlled win rate on AlpacaEval2.0 and a 6.1% relative gain in second-turn performance on a held-out MT-Bench subset versus GRPO baseline. Individual rules show good agreement with ground-truth preferences, with higher agreement on MT-Bench than UltraFeedback. Mean determinism scores are 83.6% (UltraFeedback rules) and 82.5% (MT-Bench rules). AUTORULE consistently outperforms GRPO baselines in out-of-distribution generalization, achieving ~5 percentage point improvement in AlpacaEval 2.0 win rate after two episodes. In reward hacking experiments, GRPO+LP baselines decline after step 52 while AUTORULE maintains high win rates.
limitations: Rule extraction quality depends on the reasoning model's ability to generate coherent justifications and extract meaningful rules
The binary rule satisfaction simplification may miss nuanced preference distinctions that continuous reward models capture
Rules are dataset-specific (UltraFeedback rules emphasize conversational quality, MT-Bench rules prioritize instruction adherence)
The approach was evaluated over only two training episodes in the reward hacking analysis
